Đội tuyển Việt Nam bị trừ điểm nặng sau trận thua Kyrgyzstan
Trận thua Kyrgyzstan khiến đội tuyển Việt Nam bị trừ khá nhiều điểm trên bảng xếp hạng của Liên đoàn Bóng đá thế giới (FIFA).
Bàn thua khó hiểu khiến đội tuyển Việt Nam thất bại trước Kyrgyzstan
Cầu thủ Atabaev của Kyrgyzstan đã thực hiện siêu phẩm từ giữa sân vào lưới đội tuyển Việt Nam. Bàn thua khó hiểu ở phút 88 khiến đoàn quân HLV Kim Sang Sik thất bại.
HLV Kim Sang Sik: "Trung Kiên chơi tốt trước khi mắc sai lầm ở bàn thua"
Đội tuyển Việt Nam thua ngược 1-2 trước Kyrgyzstan trên sân Thiên Trường (Ninh Bình) ở trận giao hữu quốc tế tối 17/11. Sau trận đấu, HLV Kim Sang Sik lý giải nguyên nhân đội nhà thất bại.
Tuyển Việt Nam khởi đầu thuận lợi với bàn mở tỷ số của Đình Bắc, nhưng không thể bảo toàn lợi thế và nhận thất bại 1-2 trước Kyrgyzstan, qua đó lỡ cơ hội giành chức vô địch giải đấu giao hữu.

Bảng xếp hạng Casper Cup 2026: Tuyển Việt Nam đứng thứ 2
Tuyển Việt Nam đã khép lại Giải giao hữu quốc tế Casper Cup 2026 ở vị trí thứ 2 sau thất bại 1-2 trước Kyrgyzstan tối 17-11 trên sân Thiên Trường (Ninh Bình).
Bảng xếp hạng Casper Cup 2026: Tuyển Việt Nam đứng thứ 2 - Đồ họa: THANH ĐỊNH
Sau hai trận,tuyển Việt Namgiành 3 điểm với 1 chiến thắng và 1 thất bại, ghi 3 bàn, thủng lưới 2 lần, đạt hiệu số +1. Trước đó, thầy trò ông Kim Sang Sik thắng Đài Bắc Trung Hoa 2-0 ở trận ra quân.
Kyrgyzstan giành chức vô địch với thành tích toàn thắng, thu về 6 điểm. Đại diện Trung Á ghi 5 bàn và chỉ nhận 1 bàn thua, đạt hiệu số +4. Đài Bắc Trung Hoa đứng cuối khi thua cả hai trận, không ghi được bàn nào và thủng lưới 5 lần.
Đình Bắc tiếp tục làm đội phó tuyển Việt Nam
Trước lượt cuối, tuyển Việt Nam và Kyrgyzstan cùng có 3 điểm, nhưng đội chủ nhà xếp sau vì kém hiệu số. Vì vậy, tuyển Việt Nam buộc phải thắng để đăng quang, còn đối thủ chỉ cần hòa.
Đình Bắcmang đến hy vọng cho đội chủ nhà bằng bàn mở tỉ số trong hiệp 1. Tuy nhiên, tuyển Việt Nam không bảo toàn được lợi thế và để đối phương ghi hai bàn ở những phút cuối.
Thanh Nhàn trong trận đấu với Kyrgyzstan - Ảnh: MINH ĐỖ
Valerii Kichin đánh đầu gỡ hòa từ một tình huống phạt góc. Sau đó, Erbol Atabaev tung cú sút từ phần sân nhà, đưa bóng vượt qua thủ môn Trung Kiên, ấn định chiến thắng 2-1 cho Kyrgyzstan.
Hai bàn thua cuối trận khiến tuyển Việt Nam đánh mất cơ hội giành cúp ngay trên sân nhà. Dù vậy, Casper Cup vẫn là dịp để ban huấn luyện đánh giá lực lượng, thử nghiệm đội hình và rút ra kinh nghiệm cho năm 2027.
Thua Kyrgyzstan, tuyển Việt Nam không thể vô địch Casper Cup
Tối 17-11, tại Giải giao hữu quốc tế Casper Cup 2026, tuyển Việt Nam để thua ngược 1-2 trước Kyrgyzstan và nhìn đối thủ lên ngôi vô địch.

HLV Kyrgyzstan: "Đội tuyển Việt Nam có nhiều cầu thủ giỏi" | Báo Dân trí
HLV Kyrgyzstan: "Đội tuyển Việt Nam có nhiều cầu thủ giỏi"
(Dân trí) - HLV Urmat Abdukaimov của Kyrgyzstan cho rằng đội tuyển Việt Nam có nhiều cầu thủ giỏi, nhưng chất lượng đội hình dự bị của đại diện Trung Á tốt hơn đội chủ nhà.
Tuyển Việt Nam thua ngược Kyrgyzstan, lỡ cơ hội vô địch
Đội tuyển Việt Namthua Kyrgyzstan 1-2 trong trận đấu diễn ra ở sân Thiên Trường (Ninh Bình) tối 17/11.
Nhờ trận thắng này, đội bóng Trung Á giành ngôi vô địch giải tam hùng quốc tế tại Ninh Bình.
HLV Urmat Abdukaimov của Kyrgyzstan trả lời phỏng vấn sau trận gặp đội tuyển Việt Nam (Ảnh: Đỗ Minh Quân).
Sau trận đấu, HLV Urmat Abdukaimov của Kyrgyzstan nói: “Đối thủ có nhiều cầu thủ giỏi, điều đó gây khó khăn cho chúng tôi.
Tuy nhiên, các cầu thủ Kyrgyzstan đã chơi tốt.
Chúng tôi hiếm khi phải thi đấu trong điều kiện nóng, ẩm, nhiệt độ cao như thế này”.
“Chúng tôi bỏ lỡ khá nhiều cơ hội trong hiệp một, nhưng các cầu thủ của tôi đã tận dụng cơ hội tốt hơn, biết chắt chiu cơ hội trong hiệp hai.
Toàn đội Kyrgyzstan có đấu pháp rõ ràng ngay từ đầu.
Thế nên, không thể nói chúng tôi thắng là nhờ một số tình huống cụ thể”, HLV Urmat Abdukaimov nói thêm.
Độituyển Việt Nammở tỷ số trong trận đấu này, nhờ bàn thắng của Đình Bắc ở phút 20, sau pha dứt điểm tuyệt đẹp từ ngoài khu vực 16m50.
Kyrgyzstan (áo đỏ) ngược dòng đánh bại đội tuyển Việt Nam (Ảnh: Thành Đông).
Dù vậy, trong những phút cuối trận, đội bóng đang được dẫn dắt bởi HLV Kim Sang Sik bị thủng lưới liên tiếp hai bàn ở các phút 86 và 88, trước khi chúng ta thua ngược 1-2.
Đội tuyển Kyrgyzstan nhỉnh hơn đội tuyển Việt Nam ở các nhân tố vào sân từ băng ghế dự bị.
HLV Urmat Abdukaimov của đội bóng Trung Á phân tích: “Các cầu thủ dự bị của tôi đã thay đổi kết quả trận đấu.
Đây là thành quả xứng đáng cho những nỗ lực của chúng tôi.
Phần lớn các cầu thủ Kyrgyzstan vừa kết thúc giải đấu ở trong nước, nên nhiều cầu thủ của tôi không đạt trạng thái tốt nhất khi tham gia giải năm nay”.
Kết thúc giải tam hùng quốc tế ở Ninh Bình, đội tuyển Kyrgyzstan có 6 điểm sau hai trận, giành ngôi vô địch.
Đội tuyển Việt Nam có 3 điểm sau một trận thắng và một trận thua, xếp thứ hai còn Đài Loan (Trung Quốc) không có điểm nào sau hai trận toàn thua, đứng cuối bảng.
Đội tuyển Việt Nam bị trừ điểm nặng sau trận thua Kyrgyzstan
Trận thua Kyrgyzstan khiến đội tuyển Việt Nam bị trừ khá nhiều điểm trên bảng xếp hạng của Liên đoàn Bóng đá thế giới (FIFA).
Bàn thua khó hiểu khiến đội tuyển Việt Nam thất bại trước Kyrgyzstan
Cầu thủ Atabaev của Kyrgyzstan đã thực hiện siêu phẩm từ giữa sân vào lưới đội tuyển Việt Nam.
Bàn thua khó hiểu ở phút 88 khiến đoàn quân HLV Kim Sang Sik thất bại.

lead_title: US officially loses measles-free status after 26 years amid outbreak

evidence_pages.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1:
US officially loses measles-free status after 26 years amid outbreak | Health News | Al Jazeera
Share US officially loses measles-free status after 26 years amid outbreak on social media
Add Al Jazeera on GoogleA sign reading 'measles testing' is seen as an outbreak in Gaines County, Texas, has raised concerns over its spread to other parts of the state, in Seminole, Texas, US, February 25, 2025. [Sebastian Rocandio/Reuters]ByCatherine NouhanPublished On 17 Nov 202617 Nov 2026
The United States has officially lost its measles elimination status, reversing a public health achievement maintained for 26 years, as the country grapples with its largest outbreak in more than three decades.
ThePan American Health Organization (PAHO), the Americas branch of the World Health Organization (WHO), declared measles endemic in the US, Bolivia, and Mexico on Tuesday after determining that the same strain of the virus had circulated continuously in the country for at least 12 months.

list 2 of 3CDC reports more than 5,000 measles cases, highest number in 35 years
list 3 of 3Why the US, Mexico and Guatemala may lose their measles-free status
An international panel of experts that advises PAHO on the prevalence of measles and rubella “recommended that the measles elimination status be withdrawn,” said Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, “a recommendation which I have accepted.”
Measles was declared eliminated in the US in 2000.
PAHO’s announcement follows a review of epidemiological and laboratory evidence submitted by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
The US has recorded approximately 7,700 measles infections since the beginning of 2025, according to CDC figures.
It is the highest number of cases the country has seen in more than 30 years. The climbing numbers come asvaccine hesitancy has grownunder Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, who has repeatedlycast doubt on the safety of vaccinesdespite scientific evidence to the contrary.
Before taking office, Kennedy claimed that no vaccine was “safe and effective” and promoted the discredited theory that vaccines cause autism.
To protect against illness, children are commonly given the measles vaccine in a combined shot with mumps and rubella vaccines, known by the acronym MMR.
But the vaccination rate among preschoolers in the US has fallen to about 92 percent, below the level experts say is needed to prevent major outbreaks.
As health secretary under US President Donald Trump, Kennedy has questioned the MMR vaccine’s ability to protect children.
He has suggested that the MMR’s effectiveness wanes by about 4.5 percent a year and said it contains “aborted fetus debris”,a claim experts have rejected as false.
The CDC has confirmed six measles-related deaths this year, but state health officials in Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and New York have reported 10 deaths combined, a discrepancy that has fuelledtensions between federal and state health authoritiesover how measles fatalities are classified and counted.
Measles is considered highly infectious, and the WHO credits the virus with 95,000 deaths worldwide in 2024, mostly among children.
Matt Ferrari, a biology professor and director of Pennsylvania State University’s Center for Infectious Disease Dynamics, believes the loss of the US’s measles elimination status can serve as a wake-up call for public health officials.
“This should be a humbling statement for the United States,” Ferrari told Al Jazeera.
For much of his career, Ferrari has studied strategies to control measles in countries around the world. The US was previously seen as a model.
“It was a motivating achievement that we use to drive support for measles elimination programmes all around the world,” said Ferrari. “Now we need to be looking for expertise elsewhere because we haven’t been pulling our weight.”
Edwin Asturias, a professor of paediatrics, infectious disease and epidemiology at the University of Colorado, described the loss of status as a “stain” on the country’s public health programme.
“Measles cases are a signal that your immunisation programme and other systems within your public health services are having problems,” he told Al Jazeera.
Asturias said the US had the resources and experience to prevent the resurgence of the virus, pointing to its success in eliminating local measles transmission for more than a quarter of a century.
About 40 percent of current US measles cases are among adults older than 20, he said, highlighting the need to expand vaccination efforts.
Reaching these populations will require making vaccines available in workplaces, places of worship and other community settings, rather than relying solely on paediatricians and family doctors, Asturias explained.
The loss of elimination status also hasimplications beyond US borders, as measles can spread through international travel and migration.
“The United States is not, anymore, a place where you’re safe from measles,” Asturias told Al Jazeera. “If you’re a common person walking around with your children, you need to know now that measles has come to the country to stay unless something else is done.”
The risk is particularly concerning for unvaccinated people and those who cannot receive the vaccine, including those with weakened immune systems or undergoing cancer treatment.
US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, who has repeatedly cast doubt on the safety of vaccines despite scientific evidence to the contrary [File: Evan Vucci/Reuters]
Public health experts say the announcement should serve as a catalyst for a more extensive vaccination response.
While they do not expect PAHO’s announcement to prompt a significant change in federal policy, some hope it will spur action among state and local health departments.
Ferrari argued that the US should look to countries with experience containing measles outbreaks, including India, where community health workers visit households to identify children who may have missed vaccinations or whose families may be reluctant to vaccinate.
He also suggested that states may need to reconsider vaccination strategies, including whether to offer an earlier first or second dose to protect young children in areas where measles is circulating.
In the US, children are routinely given two doses of the MMR vaccine. The first dose is typically administered to children at 12 to 15 months of age and the second at four to six years,

US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers - BBC News
BBC's Madeline Halpert explains why the US lost its measles elimination status and what it could mean.
Published17 November 2026, 16:07 GMT
After more than two decades, the US has lost its measles-free status, following two years of record case numbers and deaths.
The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a specialised service of the United Nations, determined the US has had uninterrupted transmission of the same strain of measles for more than 12 months.
Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, announced that Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles elimination status, attributing the resurgence in the region to persistent "gaps in vaccination".
The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it was committed to "regaining measles elimination status" by expanding access to vaccines.
The US has seen 5,400 cases of measles this year alone, with 10 measles-related deaths, the most the country has seen since the 1990s.
The measles virus - with its signature blotchy red rash - used to infect millions of children a year before a vaccine was invented. The extremely contagious virus can be fatal, and some patients can experience long-term complications including encephalitis and immune amnesia, which resets the immune system, leaving it with only limited ability to respond to new infections.
The US recommends two measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) shots for children between ages one and six, which is 97% effective in protecting against the illness.
PAHO, a group within the World Health Organization, revoked the US's measles-elimination after determining that the virus had circulated nonstop for more than a year.
"These figures are a serious warning for our region," PAHO's director Barbosa said at a news conference on Tuesday. "Measles is resurging globally amid persistent gaps in vaccination."
He added that Canada, which lost its status of having eliminated measles last year after seeing several large outbreaks, has made strides this year to interrupt transmission.
Daniel Salas, the executive manager of immunisations at PAHO, said that the US and others who lost elimination status would be required to submit corrective action plans outlining how they would attempt to improve vaccination rates.
US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr Kennedy has attempted to make a series of sweeping changes to US vaccine recommendations and policies. The vaccine sceptic has also frequently cast doubt on the safety of MMR shot, as vaccination rates have declined across the US in recent years.
Kennedy has argued that the rise in measles cases started before he took the helm at HHS and that neighbouring countries have also seen more infections.
Responding to Tuesday's announcement, the CDC said the agency and its partners were "committed to stopping measles outbreaks, protecting Americans, and regaining measles elimination status".
"Together, we will encourage MMR vaccination, expand access to vaccines, and help communities close gaps in protection," the agency said.
CDC Director Erica Schwartz said the measles elimination designation was not what protected Americans.
"Vaccination does," she said. "We know where transmission is occurring and we've invested $100 million in state and local health departments to reach those communities."
The UK, Spain and Austria were among European nations that lost their measles-free status earlier this year, along with countries including Russia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.
Nuwan Gunawardhana, an assistant professor of medicine with Columbia University Irving Medical Center, said the US losing its elimination status was "a huge leap backwards".
The US was the first country to eliminate measles in the Americas thanks to vaccination campaigns, noted William Moss, a paediatric infectious disease specialist at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health.
Dr Gunawardhana said it took massive efforts from public health officials and clinicians to build trust with patients to increase uptake of the MMR vaccine, leading to decades in the US with few infections and deaths.
But that trust has been steadily eroding since the Covid-19 pandemic, when Dr Gunawardhana said patients were confronted with misinformation about the safety of vaccines and lost even more trust in public health systems.
The vaccination rate for MMR across the US has fallen to 92.4%, below the 95% level that provides herd immunity, which limits the spread of measles and protects those who cannot get vaccinated, including newborns.

An outbreak in Pennsylvania has infected over 1,400 people - likely a large underestimate - and killed seven people, according to state officials.
Kennedy, the health secretary, has sparred with Pennsylvania officials over how it is counting the measles deaths, with CDC declining for now to record some of the deaths in its database.
Last year, the health secretary fired all the members of a top vaccine advisory panel and replaced them with his own appointees, some of whom were vaccine critics.
The panel recommended a number of vaccine changes - including no longer requiring the Hepatitis B vaccine for all newborns - but those recommendations were blocked by a federal judge.
President Donald Trump this year also cast doubt on the safety of the MMR vaccine, issuing an executive order for the shot to be split into three separate immunisations for measles, mumps and rubella, a move public health experts say is costly and could sow confusion about an already safe vaccine.
Doctors and public health officials say the misinformation from Kennedy and Trump has played a major role in falling vaccination rates.
"It's confusing patients. It's confusing families," Dr Gunawardhana said. "We need a clear message from the top."
The federal government's vaccine manoeuvres have left public health officials and states to fill in the gaps, offering their own separate recommendations upholding decades-long practices.

Infectious disease is now continually spreading after being eliminated for 26 years, with more than 5,400 US cases
The US lost itsmeasleselimination status, global health authorities announced, an official recognition that the infectious disease isendemic in the US after being eliminated for 26 years.
The announcement comes as the US endures the worst measles outbreak since 1991, with more than 5,400 cases and eight deaths in 2026.
“Measles is resurging globally amid the persistent gaps in vaccination coverage, and this global trend is also affecting the Americas,” said Dr Jarbas Barbosa da Silva Jr, the director of the Pan American Health Organization, a regional branch of theWorld Health Organization. “The endemic measles transmission has now been re-established in Bolivia, Mexico and United States.” Silva made the final decision on US elimination status.
A global map of WHO measles elimination status. Much of the Asian and African continents have endemic status while South and Central America as well as Australia have verified elimination status. Canada and the US have re-established measles status.
Measles is one of the most contagious viruses known to medicine and requires 95% of the community to be vaccinated to prevent outbreaks. The measles vaccine is safe and highly effective. However, pockets of low vaccination have grown in the US following pandemic-era disruptions and widespread misinformation.
The nation’s largest doctors group, the American Medical Association, described loss of measles elimination status as a “deeply troubling and entirely preventable setback for our nation”.
The loss of measles-free status comes afterDonald Trumpand his health secretary,Robert F Kennedy Jr, spent nearly two years sowing confusion about the safety of vaccines. In just one recent example, Trump called for the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) combination vaccine to be split into separate shots, arguing without evidence that “together, there could be a possibility they’re quite lethal”.

“As a pediatrician, I saw firsthand how decisions made in Washington hurt our children and families,” said Dr Annie Andrews, a Democratic senator-elect. “Nothing makes that clearer than the loss of our measles elimination status.” The loss of elimination status has already heightened criticism of Kennedy. High-profile epidemiologists called Kennedy’s work at the health department “malpractice” and equivalent to a “crime scene”.
Barbosa called the role of misinformation in measles transmission “dynamic” and urged health departments to develop bespoke campaigns tailored to under-vaccinated communities.
Experts caution against piling blame for measles outbreaks solely on theTrump administration. The MMR vaccine has been the target of misinformation for more than two decades, including work by Kennedy before his White House role.
“There is a profound problem with measles in all three North American countries,” said Noel Brewer, a behavioral scientist at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill who studies vaccination behaviors, and specifically measles. He chairs a committee that considers evidence on US measles elimination status, and contributed to the scientific work that underpinned Pan AmericanHealthOrganization (Paho)’s decision.“The US has had large outbreaks and exported those to Canada and Mexico, and those cases have come back again to the US,” said Brewer.
Canada lost its measles-free status in 2025, but Barbosa said the country now represented the “good news” in the region. The nation stopped measles transmission for 60 days. This is the first step on the way to regaining measles elimination status. TheUKand several European nations have also recentlylostelimination status.
“What we’re experiencing is not a United States specific thing,” said David Margolius of the Big Cities Health Coalition. Instead, there is a, “global surge in cases, global decline in vaccination rate”.
Public health leaders with the Big Cities Health Coalition (BHC), which leads health departments that serve 47 million Americans, described the announcement as a “profoundly sad moment for our country”.
“Recent declines in measles vaccination rates have opened the door to outbreaks across the country, resulting in preventable illness, hospitalizations, and tragic loss of life,” BHC members said in astatement. “These outcomes are especially heartbreaking because measles is a disease that we know how to prevent. Yet too many voices spreading fear and false information are exacerbating the problem.”
Expert epidemiologists recommended US measles status change duringa closed-door meeting in Washington DC. A range of evidence would have been presented, including interviews with positive patients collected by local US health authorities and whole genome sequencing that can provide a fingerprint of the virus’s origin.
Chart of countries who recently lot measles elimination status
Although measles elimination status is an official designation, it carries real consequences for Americans. Where measles cases were once typically imported by international travelers, endemic measles transmission means Americans face new risks of infection, and are being asked to dig up decades-old vaccination certificates and possibly quarantine for 21 days.
“Now is the time to go and find that evidence, because now this is a real day-to-day life thing that could happen to you,” Margoliussaidearlier in November.
Re-establishing elimination status will require “a national plan to eliminate measles again”, said Brewer, “an integrated plan that’s publicly communicated with specific tasks assigned to named parties”. He added that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the president should speak out “forcefully”in favor of vaccination, and Congress should allocate more funding.

The U.S. on Tuesday lost its official designation as a measles-free nation, more than 25 years after it eliminated the highly contagious virus.
The Pan American Health Organization announced the decision, which came after an independent panel of eight scientific expertsconvened last weekto consider the country's epidemiological evidence. The director of PAHO, the regional branch of the World Health Organization, made the final call that measles is endemic — or always present — in the U.S. following 12 months of continuous transmission.
In other words, measles is spreading regularly in the country again, with ongoing outbreaks sparking new ones.
"The commission concluded that endemic measles transmission has now been reestablished in Bolivia, Mexico, and the United States, and recommended that their measles elimination status be withdrawn — a recommendation which I have accepted," Dr. Jarbas Barbosa, PAHO director, said during a news briefing on Tuesday.
It's a devastating step backward forAmerican public health, as declining childhood vaccination rates and vaccine hesitancy fuel outbreaks across the country that have sickened thousands of people and led to a tragic string of preventable deaths. Among the deaths where vaccination status was reported, all were unvaccinated.
More than 5,400 measles caseshad been reported nationwide in 2026 as of mid-November, marking the country's worst outbreak in more than three decades. States have confirmed 10 deaths associated with the disease so far in 2026:seven in Pennsylvania, one in New York andtwo in Wisconsin.
The commission found that out of 52 U.S. states and territories it tracked, 48 experienced measles outbreaks during the reporting period between January 2025 and January 2026, PAHO Assistant Director Dr. Rhonda Sealey-Thomas said during the briefing. But Barbosa said countries are already taking action to control outbreaks, such as strengthening vaccination, surveillance and outbreak response efforts.
The U.S. in particular has ramped up vaccination efforts to close immunity gaps, particularly in areas with low immunization coverage experiencing outbreaks, said Dr. Daniel Salas, executive manager of PAHO's Special Program for Comprehensive Immunization. He said PAHO expects the U.S. to present its corrective action plan in the coming weeks, outlining strategies to regain its designation.
In a Tuesday release, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said it will continue to ensure all communities have the resources to prevent and respond to outbreaks and is committed to working with states and other local partners to restore the U.S.'s measles elimination status.
CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz said in the release the measles elimination designation "is not what protects Americans. Vaccination does." She said the agency has invested $100 million in state and local health departments to reach communities where transmission is occurring.
Last week, Schwartz told Reuters that the agency is going to be "doing the same exact thingthat we've been doing today" if the U.S. loses its measles-free status.

Kennedy Jr., who has taken steps to change recommendations for the childhood measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine and has a long history of questioning its safety without evidence.
CNBCpreviously reportedon how the return of measles in the U.S. exposes weaknesses in the nation's public health system that raise concerns about the return of other eliminated diseases. The resurgence of measles exposes eroding trust in health institutions and growing challenges in persuading people to protect themselves, their children and their communities.
Public health experts previously told CNBC that the return of measles ultimately boils down to fewer children getting vaccinated.

"We must treat the current measles outbreaks as an urgent call to rebuild trust in science-based recommendations and restore strong, fully-funded public health infrastructure to protect families and communities and prevent the return of diseases once eliminated," AMA President Dr. Willie Underwood said in a statement.

The U.S. has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, a public health triumph secured a quarter century ago.
Researchers with direct knowledge of the deliberations on the country's status told KFF Health News that the Pan American Health Organization reached the conclusion this week: Measles has reestablished regular transmission in the country.
PAHO had planned a public announcement on Nov. 17.
In public health parlance, measles elimination depends on a country's sporadic outbreaks ending within a year. That's no longer happening in the United States.
"It's a very sad moment," said Anne Schuchat, an epidemiologist and a former deputy director at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention who was not involved in PAHO's decision.
"Measles causes so much unnecessary suffering, everything from a high fever and missed work and school to long-term complications like progressive degenerative nerve disease and death," Schuchat said.
Measles outbreaks are entirely preventable: Two doses of the measles-mumps-rubella vaccine prevent about 97% of infections, so when almost everyone in a community is fully vaccinated, the virus can't spread.
In the past two years, over830 peoplehave been hospitalized with measles in the U.S. More than8,000 peoplehave been sickened in outbreaks that have cost roughly $125 million in medical care, public health response, and productivity losses,Johns Hopkins Universityresearchers estimate.
States have reported 13 measles-associated deaths, including a7-month-old in New Yorkandinfants in Pennsylvaniaand Wisconsinin recent months. Babies typically aren't vaccinated before they're a year old.
PAHO, an international group that oversees health in the Americas and works with the World Health Organization, based its assessment on two analyses: one by the CDC and another by an independent group of measles experts.
Researchers anticipated this conclusion after an outbreak in Utah surpassed the one-year mark in June.
A spokesperson for the Department of Health and Human Services, Emily Hilliard, attributed the resurgence of measles to vaccination gaps that opened years before this administration. Indeed, rates of childhood vaccination havesteadily declinedsince the COVID pandemic started.
But many scientists also blame the Trump administration for spreading vaccine misinformation and stifling a swift, strong response to outbreaks.
For example, the administrationcut millionsof dollars from children's immunization programs run by state health departments and terminated funds for research on vaccine hesitancy.
After Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. sacked CDC director Susan Monarez in August 2025, shetold Congressshe was fired because she would not preapprove changes to vaccine recommendations "without reviewing the evidence."
Monarez added that "we already have seen the largest measles outbreak in more than 30 years" and that, "if vaccine protections are weakened, preventable diseases will return."
Spokespeople for HHS and the White House defended the administration, and Kennedy, who led a prominent anti-vaccine organization before he took the helm at HHS. "The President and the Secretary have repeatedly encouraged measles vaccination, coordinated with states, and facilitated the deployment of vaccine doses across the country," White House spokesperson Allison Schuster wrote in an email.
For more than three decades, the federal government treated measles as a preventable tragedy, with sizable outbreaks triggering national efforts to boost vaccination and stop the virus from spreading.
That's no longer the case, said Patsy Stinchfield, executive director of theMeasles Collaborative, a new initiative that educates the public about vaccines and assists health workers responding to outbreaks.
Stinchfield was a pediatric nurse at a children's hospital in Minnesota during the nation's last surge of measles before elimination, from 1989 to 1991. She recalled an entire ward devoted to children with measles and the enormous effort required to prevent the virus from spreading to kids with cancer and weakened immune systems.
Two children at the hospital died of measles. "That changed my career forever," she said.
Back then, she said, the federal government "saw the urgency." Officials held press conferences, spoke on the news about vaccines, issued clinical guidelines, and published reports in the CDC's flagship journal — the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report, or MMWR — that drove policies.
When data suggested that some children weren't mounting a strong response to a single dose of the measles-mumps-rubella vaccine, a CDC advisory committee recommended two doses of the shot.
When CDC analyses found that many children with measles hadn't been vaccinated due to cost, the government launched the Vaccines for Children program to make immunizations available free of charge to underinsured families.
Cases plummeted. By 2000, the CDC and PAHO determined that measles was no longer a national threat — measles transmission had been eliminated.
"Elimination" allows for occasional outbreaks, because measles is not eradicated worldwide and a small fraction of people, such as young infants, can't be protected by vaccines.
People infected abroad sparked occasional outbreaks after U.S. elimination, but — until now — those fizzled out because of herd immunity, when 95% of people within a community are immunized. In those situations, outbreaks peter out and vulnerable people are protected.

[Sebastian Rocandio/Reuters]ByCatherine NouhanPublished On 17 Nov 202617 Nov 2026

The United States has officially lost its measles elimination status, reversing a public health achievement maintained for 26 years, as the country grapples with its largest outbreak in more than three decades.

ThePan American Health Organization (PAHO), the Americas branch of the World Health Organization (WHO), declared measles endemic in the US, Bolivia, and Mexico on Tuesday after determining that the same strain of the virus had circulated continuously in the country for at least 12 months.

An international panel of experts that advises PAHO on the prevalence of measles and rubella “recommended that the measles elimination status be withdrawn,” said Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, “a recommendation which I have accepted.”
Measles was declared eliminated in the US in 2000.
PAHO’s announcement follows a review of epidemiological and laboratory evidence submitted by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
The US has recorded approximately 7,700 measles infections since the beginning of 2025, according to CDC figures.
It is the highest number of cases the country has seen in more than 30 years.
The climbing numbers come asvaccine hesitancy has grownunder Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, who has repeatedlycast doubt on the safety of vaccinesdespite scientific evidence to the contrary.
Before taking office, Kennedy claimed that no vaccine was “safe and effective” and promoted the discredited theory that vaccines cause autism.
To protect against illness, children are commonly given the measles vaccine in a combined shot with mumps and rubella vaccines, known by the acronym MMR.
But the vaccination rate among preschoolers in the US has fallen to about 92 percent, below the level experts say is needed to prevent major outbreaks.
As health secretary under US President Donald Trump, Kennedy has questioned the MMR vaccine’s ability to protect children.
He has suggested that the MMR’s effectiveness wanes by about 4.5 percent a year and said it contains “aborted fetus debris”,a claim experts have rejected as false.

The CDC has confirmed six measles-related deaths this year, but state health officials in Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and New York have reported 10 deaths combined, a discrepancy that has fuelledtensions between federal and state health authoritiesover how measles fatalities are classified and counted.
Measles is considered highly infectious, and the WHO credits the virus with 95,000 deaths worldwide in 2024, mostly among children.

Matt Ferrari, a biology professor and director of Pennsylvania State University’s Center for Infectious Disease Dynamics, believes the loss of the US’s measles elimination status can serve as a wake-up call for public health officials.
“This should be a humbling statement for the United States,” Ferrari told Al Jazeera.
For much of his career, Ferrari has studied strategies to control measles in countries around the world.
“It was a motivating achievement that we use to drive support for measles elimination programmes all around the world,” said Ferrari.
“Now we need to be looking for expertise elsewhere because we haven’t been pulling our weight.”
Edwin Asturias, a professor of paediatrics, infectious disease and epidemiology at the University of Colorado, described the loss of status as a “stain” on the country’s public health programme.
“Measles cases are a signal that your immunisation programme and other systems within your public health services are having problems,” he told Al Jazeera.
Asturias said the US had the resources and experience to prevent the resurgence of the virus, pointing to its success in eliminating local measles transmission for more than a quarter of a century.
About 40 percent of current US measles cases are among adults older than 20, he said, highlighting the need to expand vaccination efforts.

Reaching these populations will require making vaccines available in workplaces, places of worship and other community settings, rather than relying solely on paediatricians and family doctors, Asturias explained.
The loss of elimination status also hasimplications beyond US borders, as measles can spread through international travel and migration.
“The United States is not, anymore, a place where you’re safe from measles,” Asturias told Al Jazeera.
“If you’re a common person walking around with your children, you need to know now that measles has come to the country to stay unless something else is done.”
The risk is particularly concerning for unvaccinated people and those who cannot receive the vaccine, including those with weakened immune systems or undergoing cancer treatment.
US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, who has repeatedly cast doubt on the safety of vaccines despite scientific evidence to the contrary [File: Evan Vucci/Reuters]
Public health experts say the announcement should serve as a catalyst for a more extensive vaccination response.
While they do not expect PAHO’s announcement to prompt a significant change in federal policy, some hope it will spur action among state and local health departments.

Ferrari argued that the US should look to countries with experience containing measles outbreaks, including India, where community health workers visit households to identify children who may have missed vaccinations or whose families may be reluctant to vaccinate.

Chủ tịch Liên đoàn Bóng đá Thái Lan (FAT) Madam Pang (Nualphan Lamsam) cũng không giấu được sự phấn khích sau chiến thắng của đội nhà. Trên trang cá nhân, bà đăng ảnh chụp thống kê khán giả đến sân của Ban tổ chức cùng chia sẻ ngắn gọn: "Thật tuyệt vời”.
Trong khi đó, truyền thông Thái Lan đồng loạt dành sự quan tâm đặc biệt cho thành tích của đội tuyển quốc gia.Siam Sportnhấn mạnh: “Đây là danh hiệu đầu tiên của ông Anthony Hudson trên cương vị HLV trưởng đội tuyển Thái Lan. HLV Anthony Hudson có 12 chiến thắng, 4 trận hòa và 3 thất bại sau 19 trận dẫn dắt "Voi chiến", đạt tỷ lệ thắng 63,2%”.
Siam Sportnhận xét: “Chức vô địch King's Cup 2026 là cột mốc đáng nhớ trong hành trình của Anthony Hudson. Nhà cầm quân người Anh đã giúp đội tuyển Thái Lan có thêm một danh hiệu, sau những kết quả đáng chú ý ở các giải đấu khu vực và châu lục”.
Siam Sportcũng tiết lộ: “Sau giải đấu này, đội tuyển Thái Lan sẽ trở lại thi đấu trong dịp FIFA Days từ ngày 22 đến 30.3.2027, với hai trận giao hữu đang chờ xác định đối thủ”.
Thông điệp ngắn gọn của Madam Pang sau khi đội tuyển Thái Lan vô địch King's Cup 2026
Đội tuyển Thái Lan có lần thứ 17 vô địch King's Cup
Không chỉ vui mừng vì danh hiệu, đội tuyển Thái Lan còn nhận được khoản tiền thưởng đáng kể. TờKhaosodđặc biệt chú ý đến lời hứa thưởng của Trưởng đoàn Chalermchai Mahakitjirapong trước khi giải đấu khởi tranh.
Cụ thể, theoKhaosod: “Ông Chalermchai Mahakitjirapong cam kết thưởng 3 triệu baht (khoảng 2,5 tỉ đồng) nếu đội tuyển giành chức vô địch King's Cup 2026. Đáng chú ý, khoản thưởng chưa dừng lại ở đó. Trước trận chung kết, ông Chalermchai còn tuyên bố thưởng thêm 100.000 baht (khoảng 83 triệu đồng) cho mỗi bàn thắng mà đội tuyển ghi được. Với 3 lần làm tung lưới Tajikistan, thầy trò HLV Anthony Hudson nhận thêm 300.000 baht (khoảng 250 triệu đồng). Tổng cộng, đội tuyển Thái Lan được thưởng 3,3 triệu baht, tương đương khoảng 2,75 tỉ đồng”.
Ball Thai Standcũng dành sự quan tâm đến những con số thống kê của HLV Anthony Hudson.Ball Thai Standnhắc lại: “Sau 19 trận dẫn dắt đội tuyển Thái Lan, chiến lược gia người Anh có 12 chiến thắng, 4 trận hòa và 3 thất bại, ghi được 45 bàn thắng và để thủng lưới 16 lần. Chức vô địch King's Cup lần thứ 52 tiếp tục bổ sung vào bảng thành tích của nhà cầm quân này”.
Trong khi đó,Ball Thainhấn mạnh màn trình diễn của Teerasak Pueypimai. Tiền đạo Thái Lan ghi cả hai bàn thắng trong hiệp 2, góp công lớn giúp "Voi chiến" vượt qua Tajikistan để bước lên bục cao nhất. Supachok Sarachat cũng được nhắc đến với bàn mở tỷ số quan trọng, tạo lợi thế cho đội chủ nhà sau khi đối phương mất người.

Supachok ghi bàn, đội tuyển Thái Lan vô địch King’s Cup 2026
(Dân trí) - Đánh bại đội tuyển Tajikistan với tỷ số đậm 3-0, đội tuyển Thái Lan giành King’s Cup 2026. Đây là chiến thắng đậm thứ hai của đội bóng xứ sở chùa vàng tại giải năm nay.
Trận chung kết King’s Cup năm nay diễn ra tối 17/11, trên sân vận động Sisaket (Thái Lan). Trước đội bóng Trung Á có trình độ yếu Tajikistan, đội chủ nhà Thái Lan chiếm ưu thế hoàn toàn.
Thái Lan (áo xanh) chơi áp đảo trước Tajikistan (Ảnh: FAT).
Dù chơi trên cơ, nhưng mãi đến phút 40, đội tuyển Thái Lan mới tìm được bàn mở tỷ số, do công của tiền vệ tấn công Supachok Sarachat.
Sang hiệp hai, đội tuyển Thái Lan tiếp tục tấn công mạnh. Phút 49, cách biệt được nhân đôi cho đội chủ nhà. Người ghi bàn nâng tỷ số lên 2-0 cho đội bóng xứ sở chùa vàng là tiền đạo Teerasak Poeiphimai.
Đến phút 75, Teerasak Poeiphimai ghi thêm một bàn nữa, hoàn tất cú đúp bàn thắng của mình trong trận. Đồng thời, bàn thắng này giúp cho đội tuyển Thái Lan ấn định chiến thắng 3-0.
Thái Lan giành King's Cup 2026 (Ảnh: FAT).
Chiến thắng này giúp cho đội bóng xứ sở chùa vàng đoạt ngôi vô địch giải đấu truyền thống được tổ chức trên sân nhà.
Đây cũng là trận thắng thứ hai của Thái Lan tại King’s Cup 2026. Họ ghi được tổng cộng 9 bàn thắng qua hai trận, không để thủng lưới bàn nào. Tuy nhiên, việc đội tuyển Thái Lan thắng đậm hai trận đã qua, chủ yếu vì đối thủ của họ quá yếu.
Cụ thể, Thái Lan thắng đội tuyển Brunei 6-0 ở bán kết vào ngày 14/11 và thắng Tajikistan 3-0 ở chung kết ngày 17/11.
Thái Lan vào chung kết King’s Cup, Malaysia thua đội tuyển Trung Quốc
Giành chiến thắng đậm 6-0 trước Brunei tối 14/11, đội tuyển Thái Lan giành quyền vào chơi trận chung kết King’s Cup 2026. Ở trận đấu giao hữu cùng giờ, Malaysia thua 0-2 trước đội tuyển Trung Quốc.

Sau hai thất bại trước U23 Việt Nam và U23 Qatar, U23 Thái Lan đã giành chiến thắng 3-1 trước U23 Singapore. Đáng chú ý, siêu phẩm của Paripan Wongsa khiến nhiều người ngỡ ngàng.

Tìm ra hai đội vô địch giải thể thao điện tử FanG Campus 2026 - Báo VnExpress Thể thao
Tìm ra hai đội vô địch giải thể thao điện tử FanG Campus 2026
Trường đại học Công nghệ Thông tin và Truyền thông Việt Hàn vô địch Liên Quân Mobile trong khi Trường đại học Văn Hiến thắng môn Valorant tại FanG Campus.
Giải đấu thể thao điện tử thế hệ số toàn quốc (FanG Campus) là giải đấu thể thao điện tử được tổ chức bởi FPT Play với mục tiêu xây dựng môi trường thi đấu, giao lưu và kết nối cộng đồng người chơi. Chương trình có sự đồng hành của Cục An ninh mạng - Bộ Công An và Cục Thể dục Thể thao Việt Nam - Bộ Văn hóa, Thể thao và Du lịch. 64 đội tuyển đến từ 32 trường đại học, cao đẳng trên toàn quốc thi đấu vòng loại. 4 đội xuất sắc quy tụ tại Chung kết toàn quốc diễn ra trong hai ngày 14-15/11 tại Đại học Phenikaa, Hà Nội.
Giải đấu thể thao điện tử thế hệ số toàn quốc 2026. Ảnh:FPT Play
Giải đấu có tổng giải thưởng 300 triệu đồng, gồm 60 triệu đồng tiền mặt, 240 triệu đồng quà tặng.
Ở bộ mônLiên Quân Mobile, Đại học Phenikaa và Trường Đại học Công nghệ Thông tin và Truyền thông Việt - Hàn đối đầu trong trận chung kết. Trường Đại học Công nghệ Thông tin và Truyền thông Việt - Hàn đã giành chiến thắng chung cuộc, trở thành nhà vô địch.
Trong khi đó, chung kếtValorantgiữa Đại học Phenikaa và Trường Đại học Văn Hiến trở thành cuộc rượt đuổi tỷ số căng thẳng. Trường Đại học Văn Hiến đã vượt qua đối thủ để giành chức vô địch với tỉ số 3-2.
Nhà vô địch bộ môn Valorant tại Chung kết toàn quốc FanG Campus 2026. Ảnh:FPT Play
Xuyên suốt giải đấu và các buổi offline chung kết ghi nhận 1.500 lượt người tham dự trực tiếp, đồng thời đạt hàng triệu lượt xem và tương tác trên các nền tảng.
Ông Kim Cang, Giám đốc Ban Dự án eSports, FPT Play cho biết FanG Campus 2026 là dấu mốc đáng nhớ khi đơn vị lần đầu tiên triển khai một giải đấu thể thao điện tử có quy mô toàn quốc. "Giải đã kết nối các đội tuyển và cộng đồng yêu thích esports trên nhiều tỉnh, thành", ông Cang nói.
Song song thi đấu, FanG Campus 2026 triển khai chuỗi hội thảo chuyên đề về an toàn, an ninh mạng nhằm nâng cao nhận thức của sinh viên và kết nối cộng đồng eSports. Hoạt động triển khai tại FPT Polytechnic Hà Nội, Trường Đại học Xây dựng Hà Nội, Trường Đại Học Công Nghệ TP HCM (HUTECH), Greenwich Việt Nam, Đại học Phenikaa và FPT Polytechnic Đà Nẵng.
Trung tá Đinh Quang Vũ, Phó giám đốc Trung tâm huấn luyện và Đại úy Trần Đức Mạnh, Chuyên viên Trung tâm huấn luyện thuộc Cục An ninh mạng (Bộ Công an) với vai trò diễn giả đã trực tiếp minh họa cách thức những chiêu trò lừa đảo được xây dựng và vận hành. Diễn giả lý giải vì sao các thủ đoạn này có thể đánh lừa cả những người trẻ thường xuyên sử dụng công nghệ, đồng thời hướng dẫn phương pháp phòng tránh và xử lý.
Trung tá Đinh Quang Vũ, Phó giám đốc Trung tâm huấn luyện, Cục An ninh mạng cảnh báo nguy cơ an ninh mạng tại Đại học HUTECH. Ảnh:FPT Play
Chuỗi hoạt động được đón nhận tích cực nhờ nội dung thiết thực, gần gũi với những tình huống thường gặp trong môi trường số.
FanG Campus 2026 nhận được sự đồng hành của nhiều đơn vị đơn hoạt động trong lĩnh vực thể thao điện tử trong đó có VNGGames và Garena, giúp kết nối giải đấu với cộng đồng người chơi của hai game. Giải còn có sự đồng hành của Logitech hay MSI.
Samsung Odyssey tham gia giải đấu với vai trò Đối tác đồng hành chính thức, góp phần nâng cao trải nghiệm thi đấu và giải trí cho các đội tuyển. Toàn bộ màn hình thi đấu tại sự kiện Chung kết miền và Chung kết toàn quốc dành cho bộ môn Valorant sử dụng thiết bị Samsung.
Màn hình Samsung được sử dụng tại sự kiện Chung kết miền và Chung kết toàn quốc bộ môn Valorant. Ảnh:FPT Play
Bà Huyền My, Giám đốc Ngành hàng Điện tử Tiêu dùng, Công ty Điện tử Samsung Việt Nam, đánh giá FanG Campus 2026 là sân chơi có tính cạnh tranh, nhiều cảm xúc. Màn hình Samsung Odyssey góp phần hỗ trợ game thủ thể hiện tốt nhất trong những trận đấu quan trọng.
"Chúng tôi kỳ vọng chứng kiến sự phát triển và hưởng ứng ngày càng lớn của cộng đồng đối với sân chơi thể thao điện tử như FanG Campus."
Thông qua mùa giải đầu tiên, FPT Play cho biết kỳ vọng phát triển những hoạt động kết nối eSports gắn với giá trị cộng đồng, góp phần thúc đẩy phong trào thể thao điện tử lành mạnh. Đơn vị đồng thời lan tỏa nhận thức về an toàn thông tin, văn hóa ứng xử và trách nhiệm của mỗi cá nhân khi tham gia không gian mạng.

A mysterious twist in the universe’s oldest light could reveal new physics
Date:November 17, 2026Source:University of California - San DiegoSummary:Scientists have spotted hints of a mysterious rotation in the universe’s oldest light that could reveal new physics and shed light on dark matter and dark energy. A new technique developed at UC San Diego could help rule out misleading telescope errors, bringing researchers closer to determining whether the strange signal is real.Share:FacebookTwitterPinterestLinkedINEmailFULL STORYA mysterious twist in light from the Big Bang could reveal hidden physics, and scientists have developed a new way to test whether the signal is real. Credit: AI/ScienceDaily.com
A mysterious twist in the universe's oldest light could offer clues to physics that scientists have yet to discover. But before researchers can determine whether this subtle signal reveals something extraordinary about the cosmos, they must answer a crucial question: Is the effect actually coming from the universe, or could it be an illusion created by the telescopes observing it?
The mystery centers on the cosmic microwave background (CMB), a faint glow of radiation left over from approximately 380,000 years after the Big Bang. This ancient light provides a remarkable snapshot of the "baby universe" as it existed nearly 13.8 billion years ago, allowing scientists to investigate conditions from the earliest stages of cosmic history.
When the universe was about 380,000 years old, it had cooled enough to become transparent, allowing light to travel freely through space. As radiation scattered off free electrons during this transition, it acquired a small amount of linear polarization. Polarization describes the direction in which light's electric field oscillates, and a similar effect occurs when sunlight scatters through Earth's atmosphere.
Now, observations suggest that the polarization of this ancient radiation may have shifted slightly as the light traveled across the universe. This possible rotation, called cosmic birefringence, is especially intriguing because it could point to physical processes not explained by the Standard Model, the leading theory describing fundamental particles and their interactions. Confirming the effect might even provide new insights into dark matter and dark energy (see Sidebar).
A Mysterious Cosmic Signal or a Telescope Error?
There is a major obstacle to interpreting this potential discovery. An extremely small error in how a telescope's polarization detectors are aligned can produce a signal that looks almost identical to cosmic birefringence.
To help address this problem, physicists at the University of California San Diego developed a new technique for checking how accurately different groups of detectors measure polarization angles. They tested their approach using existing observations collected by the European Space Agency's Planck satellite, which mapped the universe's ancient radiation in extraordinary detail.
The research was led by Postdoctoral Fellow Anto I. Lonappan, Chancellor's Distinguished Professor of Physics Brian Keating, and Associate Professor of Physics Kam Arnold. Their findings were published inThe Astrophysical Journal Letters.
Separating Real Cosmic Effects From Instrument Errors
Previous studies have suggested that the polarization of the CMB may have rotated by just a fraction of a degree over its nearly 14 billion years of travel. Although that sounds insignificant, such a tiny change could have enormous implications for fundamental physics.
Unfortunately, a telescope whose polarization detectors are misaligned by a similarly small angle could produce precisely the same apparent rotation. If every detector shares the same alignment error, the resulting measurements cannot distinguish that error from a genuine rotation of the cosmic signal.
The UC San Diego researchers found a way to investigate the problem from another angle. Rather than relying on a single combined measurement, they compared separate polarization maps generated by different groups of detectors.
If cosmic birefringence is real, its effect should appear consistently across all these maps. By comparing the maps with one another, the researchers can effectively eliminate any rotation shared by all of them. What remains reveals differences in the calibration of the individual detector groups, making it possible to identify inconsistencies that might otherwise complicate the search for new physics.
"The signal we are looking for is incredibly small, so we have to be certain that we are seeing the universe and not our instrument," said Lonappan. "Our method gives us a complementary way to check that distinction. Before interpreting a tiny rotation as new physics, we want to know that the calibration itself can be trusted."
Testing the Mystery With Planck Satellite Data
To evaluate their technique, the researchers analyzed eight polarization maps produced using Planck observations. They then compared their findings with results from an established approach called the Minami-Komatsu analysis, which is used to distinguish instrumental rotation from possible cosmic birefringence.
Although the two methods rely on different assumptions, they produced consistent results. This agreement provides an important independent check on how relative detector calibration errors are being assessed.
The new approach also has a deliberate limitation. Because it removes any rotation common to all the maps, it cannot independently measure the overall polarization angle or determine how much the universe itself may have rotated the light. Establishing that absolute rotation still requires an independent reference for calibrating the overall angle.
To demonstrate how their findings fit with existing measurements, the researchers combined their reconstruction of relative calibration differences with the common calibration value inferred from the established analysis. This produced an estimated cosmic birefringence angle of 0.37 ± 0.12 degrees, matching the Minami-Komatsu result.
Importantly, this agreement does not independently confirm that the ancient light has actually rotated. Instead, it shows that the new method can reproduce results from the existing framework while providing a separate way to examine potential calibration problems.

Mysterious object in space: Could it be a Soviet probe missing for 40 years? | Euronews
ByEuronews Farsi teamPublished on15 November 2026 - 17:34 GMT+1ShareCommentsAdd Euronews on GoogleShareFacebookTwitterFlipboardSendRedditLinkedinMessengerTelegramVKBlueskyThreadsWhatsapp
The object, known as "1998 KY26", about 11 metres wide, is moving near Earth; yet something other than the Sun's or Earth's gravity seems to affect its path and speed.
A mysterious object speeding through the Solar System has shown unusual acceleration, raising speculation that it could be a spacecraft from the former Soviet Union that went missing nearly 40 years ago.
Known as 1998 KY26, the object is an 11-metre-wide body passing near Earth. Scientists have noticed that its trajectory cannot be fully explained by the gravitational pull of the Sun or Earth.
This unusual behaviour is known as "non-gravitational acceleration", meaning that forces other than gravity are influencing the object's path and speed.
NASA chief Jared Isaacman said on Thursday that the agency is monitoring KY26 but stressed there is no reason for concern. He reassured the public that the object poses no known threat to Earth and that there is no evidence it could collide with our planet.
A group of researchers has put forward an unusual explanation. Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb and two colleagues, Adam Hibberd and Adam Crowl, believe KY26 could be Phobos 1, an unmanned Soviet spacecraft launched on 7 July 1988. The probe lost contact with Earth while on its way to Mars.
The researchers built a simplified model of Phobos 1 and compared how it would reflect sunlight as it rotated with observations of KY26. They found that the model closely matched eight separate sets of observations of the object.
KY26 reflects almost 52% of the sunlight that hits it and completes one full rotation every 5.35 minutes. Loeb and his colleagues argue that these characteristics are consistent with their hypothesis that KY26 could be an artificial object.
Watch: SpaceX catches Starship in midair on return to launch tower
New study challenges the dark comet theory
One explanation, first proposed in a 2023 study, is that KY26 is a so-called 'dark comet' containing trapped water that turns into gas, creating thrust as the object moves through space. However, astronomers have not detected the cloud of gas or tail normally associated with comets.
A separate scientific study has offered a contrasting explanation. Researchers concluded that 1998 KY26 is most likely a dehydrated asteroid. This would mean that water ice is unlikely to be responsible for its unusual acceleration, as temperatures are too high for sufficient ice to survive over an extended period.
Another possible explanation is solar radiation, which can exert pressure on the object's surface and slightly alter its trajectory.
Other observations also point towards a natural, rocky asteroid rather than an old spacecraft. A study published in the journalNature Communicationsin 2025 estimated its diameter at just 11 metres.
Japanese spacecraft could solve the mystery
A Japanese space mission could eventually provide important answers. The Hayabusa2 spacecraft is due to reach 1998 KY26 in July 2031 and study it at close range. It would be the first mission to directly investigate an asteroid of this tiny size.
Images and measurements taken during the encounter could reveal whether the object is indeed a natural rocky body or potentially something artificial.
Until then, Avi Loeb's suggestion remains a fascinating but unproven theory. The Harvard astrophysicist has even joked that Hayabusa2's cameras might discover a label reading "Made in the U.S.S.R." rather than a block of ice.

Ed Miliband announces first sanctions on Israeli firms working in West Bank | West Bank | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
Israeli police stand guard near the settlement of Maale Adummim, in a land corridor known as E1, outside Jerusalem in the occupied West BankPhotograph: Menahem Kahana/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenIsraeli police stand guard near the settlement of Maale Adummim, in a land corridor known as E1, outside Jerusalem in the occupied West BankPhotograph: Menahem Kahana/AFP/Getty Images
Ed Miliband announces first sanctions on Israeli firms working in West Bank
Move is designed to hinder building of more illegal settlements, which Foreign Office says Israel has ‘refused to clamp down on’
Ed Miliband has announced the first set of sanctions against Israeli companies planning to build illegal settlements in the West Bank, after he pledged to try to prevent settlements that destroy the chances of a two-state solution.
The UK foreign secretary also announced he was placing sanctions on a rightwing activist Israeli group involved in trying to block aid into Gaza as recently as last month.
Miliband announced the measures just before tenders for the large E1West Banksettlement were due to be allocated by the Israeli government, while saying he wanted to work with a new Israeli government in a more cooperative way.
View image in fullscreenGadi Eisenkot and Benjamin Netanyahu at the Knesset on 10 November.Photograph: Amir Levy/Getty Images
Israel’s possible new prime minister, Gadi Eisenkot has said that, if appointed, he will take a tougher approach than Benjamin Netanyahu to settler violence.
The sanctions are designed to stop the flow of finance to eight identified construction firms, although in practice the extent to which any of the firms are dependent on British finance is yet to be tested.
On 8 September, Milibandannounced an expansionof its Global Human Rights sanctions regime, as well as a complex set of measures, yet to be implemented, designed to ban the trade in goods from illegal settlements. The Foreign Office said that it welcomed and encouraged trade with “green line Israel” and firmly distinguished this with activity in settlements.
View image in fullscreenPalestinian children at a makeshift school established inside tents in Gaza City.Photograph: Omar Ashtawy/HL/Getty Images
The Foreign Office said the current Israeli government had “not only refused to clamp down on illegal settlement, but has facilitated and encouraged them”. More settlements had been approved under the four years of this Israeli government than in the previous 20 years.
The entities targeted by sanctions are Israeli construction, property development and architectural businesses that have helped to plan, build, supply or market housing and public infrastructure in Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
Miliband – who was criticised by some for broadening the sanctions criteria and planning a ban on trade with illegal settlement – said: “Protecting the two-state solution is the north star of this government’s approach.
“That is why my message on E1 is clear: do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution. And we will not stand by while those blocking desperately needed aid deepen the intolerable suffering of civilians in Gaza. The status quo in the West Bank and Gaza is unacceptable.”
‘The cold is lethal’: storms leave thousands in Gaza without shelterRead more
But he added in a potential olive branch: “We are committed to working productively with a new Israeli government and the Palestinian Authority to advance lasting peace and security for Israelis and Palestinians alike.”
Miliband and his Middle East minister, Stephen Doughty, have repeatedly highlighted the Israeli government’s refusal to let a variety of dual-use goods into Gaza. The Foreign Office said civilians in Gaza were in desperate need of winter supplies, with catastrophic floods leaving nearly 4,000 households without shelter and 1.4 million people living in tents or makeshift shelters.
View image in fullscreenThe separation wall near the E1 area of the occupied West Bank, where Israel is planning more settlements.Photograph: Ohad Zwigenberg/AP
According to the UN, more than 150,000 tents and 300,000 tarpaulins bought by humanitarian partners and donors are outside Gaza ready to go in, but are being held by the Israeli authorities. The Israeli authorities also continue to block timber from entering, leaving no emergency shelter kits available in Gaza.
The Israeli government claims the blockage of some goods is necessary to prevent Hamas obtaining items that could be used to attack Israel. The dispute over dual-use goods and closed entry points into Gaza has lasted for more than two years.

Israeli police stand guard near the settlement of Maale Adummim, in a land corridor known as E1, outside Jerusalem in the occupied West BankPhotograph: Menahem Kahana/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenIsraeli police stand guard near the settlement of Maale Adummim, in a land corridor known as E1, outside Jerusalem in the occupied West BankPhotograph: Menahem Kahana/AFP/Getty Images
Ed Miliband announces first sanctions on Israeli firms working in West Bank
Move is designed to hinder building of more illegal settlements, which Foreign Office says Israel has ‘refused to clamp down on’

Ed Miliband has announced the first set of sanctions against Israeli companies planning to build illegal settlements in the West Bank, after he pledged to try to prevent settlements that destroy the chances of a two-state solution.
The UK foreign secretary also announced he was placing sanctions on a rightwing activist Israeli group involved in trying to block aid into Gaza as recently as last month.

Miliband announced the measures just before tenders for the large E1West Banksettlement were due to be allocated by the Israeli government, while saying he wanted to work with a new Israeli government in a more cooperative way.
View image in fullscreenGadi Eisenkot and Benjamin Netanyahu at the Knesset on 10 November.Photograph: Amir Levy/Getty Images
Israel’s possible new prime minister, Gadi Eisenkot has said that, if appointed, he will take a tougher approach than Benjamin Netanyahu to settler violence.

The sanctions are designed to stop the flow of finance to eight identified construction firms, although in practice the extent to which any of the firms are dependent on British finance is yet to be tested.

On 8 September, Milibandannounced an expansionof its Global Human Rights sanctions regime, as well as a complex set of measures, yet to be implemented, designed to ban the trade in goods from illegal settlements.
The Foreign Office said that it welcomed and encouraged trade with “green line Israel” and firmly distinguished this with activity in settlements.
View image in fullscreenPalestinian children at a makeshift school established inside tents in Gaza City.Photograph: Omar Ashtawy/HL/Getty Images
The Foreign Office said the current Israeli government had “not only refused to clamp down on illegal settlement, but has facilitated and encouraged them”.
More settlements had been approved under the four years of this Israeli government than in the previous 20 years.

The entities targeted by sanctions are Israeli construction, property development and architectural businesses that have helped to plan, build, supply or market housing and public infrastructure in Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

Miliband – who was criticised by some for broadening the sanctions criteria and planning a ban on trade with illegal settlement – said: “Protecting the two-state solution is the north star of this government’s approach.
“That is why my message on E1 is clear: do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution.
And we will not stand by while those blocking desperately needed aid deepen the intolerable suffering of civilians in Gaza.
The status quo in the West Bank and Gaza is unacceptable.”
‘The cold is lethal’: storms leave thousands in Gaza without shelterRead more

But he added in a potential olive branch: “We are committed to working productively with a new Israeli government and the Palestinian Authority to advance lasting peace and security for Israelis and Palestinians alike.”
Miliband and his Middle East minister, Stephen Doughty, have repeatedly highlighted the Israeli government’s refusal to let a variety of dual-use goods into Gaza.

The Foreign Office said civilians in Gaza were in desperate need of winter supplies, with catastrophic floods leaving nearly 4,000 households without shelter and 1.4 million people living in tents or makeshift shelters.
View image in fullscreenThe separation wall near the E1 area of the occupied West Bank, where Israel is planning more settlements.Photograph: Ohad Zwigenberg/AP
According to the UN, more than 150,000 tents and 300,000 tarpaulins bought by humanitarian partners and donors are outside Gaza ready to go in, but are being held by the Israeli authorities.
The Israeli authorities also continue to block timber from entering, leaving no emergency shelter kits available in Gaza.
The Israeli government claims the blockage of some goods is necessary to prevent Hamas obtaining items that could be used to attack Israel.
The dispute over dual-use goods and closed entry points into Gaza has lasted for more than two years.

Mike McCormick, a former FAA senior executive and air traffic manager, told Hernandez that he thinks another nationwide ground stop is unlikely. It's the first time those three have had a joint summit. The meeting will happen on the sidelines of the APEC summit that Xi is hosting in Shenzhen.

Shivaram says that Europe and Ukraine are concerned abouthow Ukraine may be discussedat the meeting, and what might come out of it, because President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will not be at APEC and Trump has recently been more lenient toward Putin and Russia.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation has shaken Silicon Valley, prompting calls from some tech leaders for the board to reinstate him. Trump said he agreed with them. Meanwhile, the U.S. government introduced a rule toblock remote access to advanced AI chipsand servers, closing a loophole that could allow adversarial governments to access American AI technology through overseas data centers. Nvidia is the world's dominant producer of AI chips.

An online petition supporting his reinstatement hasgarnered more than 160,000 signatures, but Bond says some of them may not be real. Elon Musk says he signed it. Brad Gerstner from Altimeter Capital, a key Nvidia investor, has urged the board to thoroughly investigate and keep all options open. Bond says the interim CEO and CFO will address the public for the first time following today's earnings report.

Although there was speculation about potentially reducing the charges to manslaughter or second-degree murder after her previous trial ended in a mistrial, no changes were made during Monday's court hearing. Judge William Sullivan, who presided over the first trial, will oversee the new proceedings. He denied Clancy's defense team's request to dismiss the charges based on double jeopardy. One year ago, New Mexico became the first state to offer free childcare to all families regardless of income, as long as adults are working, seeking work, in school, or unable to work. Many parents have found this initiative life-changing, but capacity was limited. Only 50% of the some 67,000 children ages 5 and under are enrolled in the universal childcare program. Some of the remaining families participate in other programs, such as PreK and Head Start. New Mexico officials say the program must expand to meet demand. The issues observed in New Mexico are mirrored across the nation, prompting policymakers and childcare advocates toclosely monitor the state's initiative.
👶 Almost half of U.S. children aged 5 and under live in licensed childcare deserts, where demand exceeds availability, according to the Center for American Progress, a left-leaning think tank.
👶 New Mexico's program has an operating budget of nearly $600 million, but some lawmakers are concerned it could be $50 million over budget this year.
👶 New Mexico state Sen. Steve Lanier tells NPR that the steep cost of the program is why he only supports universal childcare for some people, since someone earning around $450,000 or $600,000 might not need assistance. Lanier has previously sued to end the initiative, but the lawsuit was unsuccessful.
👶 Since the enactment of free, universal childcare in New Mexico, lower-income mothers have experienced significant gains. Their full-time employment has risen by 23%, according to a new paper from Arizona State University.

Trump to embark on Asia trip in apparent foreign policy push before end of term | Donald Trump | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
‘The president has been badly damaged by the election and will have limited prospects for the next two years,’ said one China specialist.Photograph: Evan Vucci/ReutersView image in fullscreen‘The president has been badly damaged by the election and will have limited prospects for the next two years,’ said one China specialist.Photograph: Evan Vucci/Reuters
Trump to embark on Asia trip in apparent foreign policy push before end of term
Experts say US president may lean toward global affairs after domestic influence curtailed in midterm elections
Donald Trump is embarking on his first overseas trip since his Republican party’s thumping midterm repudiation by US voters, in what may herald a renewed focus on foreign policy for the remainder of his presidency.
The US president will meet his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, for their first trilateral summit, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) forum in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. Before that, he will land in Manila in the Philippines on Tuesday for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit.
At the Asean summit, Trump is expected to sign a trade agreement withThailand, push deals with other countries and lobby fellow leaders to favour the US over China on artificial intelligence.
He will also take part in the first leaders’ meeting of the Quad partnership – consisting of the US, Japan, India and Australia – since he returned to the White House in January 2025.
White House officials said the president would be accompanied to Apec by Elon Musk, the Tesla and SpaceX entrepreneurwho spent almost $500m(£380m) unsuccessfully supporting Republican candidates in this month’s midterms. The reason for Musk’s presence has not been explained.
The China leg of the trip will take place amid the continuing fallout from theNvidia spying scandal, which prompted the company’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, to resign amid revelations he had had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
Trump is under pressure to raise the matter with Xi when they hold a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of Apec.
The US president hassaid he does not plan to bring up the subject; administration officials insist he will not do so and that the meeting will be dedicated to implementing a trade agreement between the two superpowers.
Huang persuaded theTrump administrationto lift restrictions on the sale of Nvidia’s AI chips to China that had been imposed during Joe Biden’s presidency.
Mao Ning, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson, told reporters on Monday that at the trilateral summit, Xi, Trump and Putin “will exchange views in depth on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations, which is of groundbreaking significance”.
View image in fullscreenA sign in Shenzen’s business district promoting the Apec summit.Photograph: Alex Plavevski/EPA
Some analysts have characterised the meetingas a “big three” gathering echoing the 1945 Yalta meeting of Winston Churchill, Franklin D Roosevelt and Joseph Stalin that in effect carved up postwar Europe, between a communist-ruled east and a democratic, capitalist west.
Such a prospect has alarmedUkraine, which fears that Putin – who initially suggested the trilateral meeting – will use it to persuade Trump and Xi to agree to a settlement of the war with Russia on Moscow’s terms.
However, Trump has said Ukraine will not be up for debate at the meeting and that its main purpose will be to discuss ending the US’s war with Iran and “denuclearisation” – shorthand for a deal among the three powers to limit nuclear arms.
That is believed to be unpalatable toChina, which has been increasing its nuclear arsenal, and has signalled an unwillingness to enter into reduction agreements until it is closer to parity with the US and Russia.
Analysts say the main beneficiary of the three-way meeting is likely to be Putin, whose standing will be boosted by being treated on an equal footing by two other leaders whose countries are, in reality, much more powerful.
Expectations of a substantial agreement are low.
Lyle Goldstein, an international affairs fellow and China specialist at Brown University in the US, said the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting would not have a substantive result. “There will be no ‘Yalta’, as many have feared,” he said.
Jonathan Czin, the Michael Armacost chair in foreign policy studies at the Brookings Institution, said Trump’s lame duck status would deter Xi and Putin from trying to reach long-term arrangements with the US.
“Both men know Trump’s time is expiring even more quickly than his leverage – and that he will be irrelevant in a mere 26 months [when his term expires],” Czin told anonline Brookings forum. “Why would either man make a deal with a leader whose time and leverage are waning? They will only do it if they think they can pilfer more from Trump diplomatically than they will be able to gain from the next American president.”
Nevertheless, Goldstein – who took soundings on Chinese expectations for the summit in a visit to Shenzhen last week – predicted Trump would follow the pattern of previous presidents by turning increasingly to global affairs while he faces the prospect of his influence on the domestic front being curtailed after the Democrats’ victories in the House of Representatives and the Senate.
“The president has been badly damaged by the election and will have limited prospects for the next two years,” he said. “That may cause him to be more active in foreign policy since he can act in that domain with fewer constraints. It would not surprise me if Trump is ready to go all-out to make some further splash in foreign policy.”
With the risks of reigniting the war with Iran high and the Russia-Ukraine war still resistant to a diplomatic resolution despite White House efforts, Goldstein suggested Trump could attempt “a dramatic foreign policy flourish in Asia”, such as an agreement with Kim Jong-un, the North Korean dictator with whom he has frequently boasted of having a close relationship. Kim is not expected to attend the Apec gathering, although there have been rumours he may appear.
